title: ThIDE scene plan, version 1
description: A resolved description of one render, played in Blender by the ThIDE player. Positions are metres in one frame (X east, Y north, Z up) about frame.origin; times are seconds from the start of the clip; colours are linear RGB, each channel 0 to 1. Unknown top-level sections are allowed: they belong to player modules outside this schema. Every other object is closed: the player and the library refuse a key it does not list, which may be one a newer version added.

features.description: The player modules the plan needs, in the order they run. A player without one of them refuses the plan. A movie of several scenes has segments, texts and output and no other (see 'segments'). The player's own: models, lines, camera_track, look, textured_materials, labels, annotations, changes, texts, blend_file, output.

moduleFolders.description: Folders beside the plan that hold more modules, as paths relative to the plan.

frame.description: The coordinate frame of every position in the plan.

origin.description: Where the plan's origin lies in the world: world = plan + origin.

crs.description: The coordinate system of the origin.

timeline.description: The length of the clip. Time 0 is frame 1; a time t falls on frame 1 + round(t * fps).

id.description: The model's name in the scene; unique in the plan.

role.description: What the model is, for whoever looks for it in the scene. Default 'model'.

path.description: A .ply or .glb file, relative to the plan.

translation.description: Where the mesh's own origin lies in the frame.

rotation.description: A turn of the mesh about its own origin, by the right-hand rule: about [0, 0, 1], 90 degrees turn east to north.

axis.description: The direction of the axis; any length but zero.

scale.description: A stretch along the mesh's own X, Y and Z axes, applied before the rotation. Default [1, 1, 1].

material.description: The id of one of look.materials. Without it the model keeps what its file brings.

lines.description: Played by the module 'lines', before 'look': lines drawn through given points as thin tubes, which the player builds: the legs of a survey, a route, an outline. In everything else a line is a model: it is placed as one, it wears the material of look.materials it names, and 'changes' change it as they change a model. Ids are unique among models and lines.

id.description: The line's name in the scene; unique among models and lines.

role.description: What the line is, for whoever looks for it in the scene. Default 'line'.

width.description: How thick the line is, in metres.

material.description: The id of one of look.materials: the line's colour (flat), a ramp over height, or the colours of its points (vertexColor).

translation.description: As for a model: where the line's own origin lies in the frame. Default [0, 0, 0]: the points are in the plan's frame.

strips.description: The runs of the line. Either every strip gives its points colours or none does, and the same of reveal values.

points.description: Where the strip runs, in order; two points are one straight piece.

colors.description: A colour for every point; the line blends from one to the next. Shown by a material of the kind vertexColor.

reveal.description: A reveal value for every point: what a change's 'reveal' shows the line by, part by part. Between two points the line is there up to where the threshold has got to between their values. Either every strip of a line has them or none has.

sensorWidth.description: Millimetres; with the lens it gives the horizontal field of view. Default 36.

fStop.description: Turns depth of field on, focused on the target.

track.description: The poses, in rising order of time. One pose is a camera that stands still. Either every pose has an orientation or none has.

clipStart.description: The nearest the camera draws at this pose. Default: the camera's clipStart. Between poses it moves as the camera does, so a flight from far away to close by keeps its depth exact at both ends.

clipEnd.description: The farthest the camera draws at this pose. Default: the camera's clipEnd.

orientation.description: How the camera is turned, as a unit quaternion [w, x, y, z] in the plan's frame; the camera looks along its own -Z with its own +Y at the top of the picture, so [1, 0, 0, 0] looks straight down with north up. With it the camera keeps this turn, roll included, and the target is only where it focuses; without it the camera looks at the target with a level horizon. Blender interpolates the turn as the track's interpolation says.

engine.description: workbench is Blender's solid view, for a draft: no lights, shadows or noise; every model in the colours of its material, a ramp over height included. Default cycles.

samples.description: For workbench the anti-aliasing: 1 is none, up to 4 a fast approximation, then the largest of 5, 8, 11, 16 and 32 that it reaches.

device.description: For Cycles; falls back to the CPU.

color.description: The colour of a flat material, and of a vertexColor one on a mesh without colours.

stops.description: The colours of a heightRamp or a noiseRamp, in rising order of 'at'.

low.description: The height (Z) where a heightRamp starts.

high.description: The height where a heightRamp ends.

space.description: Where a heightRamp measures 'low' and 'high'. scene (the default): in the plan's frame, so a model that is stretched or moved passes through the colours. model: in the model's own coordinates, as its file has them, before its scale, rotation and translation, so a colour stays with the rock it is on.

scale.description: Of a noiseRamp's noise; larger is finer.

bump.description: How strongly a noiseRamp's noise bumps the surface.

banded.description: True for a ramp in bands: the colour of a stop holds from the stop up to the next one, and changes there at once, where a ramp otherwise blends from stop to stop. Default false.

unlit.description: True for a material that no light changes: it shows the colours of its kind as a screen shows them, in a cave no lamp reaches as under the sun, and lights nothing itself. For what has to read at any distance: survey lines, a route. Roughness has no part in it. Default false.

strength.description: How brightly an unlit material shows its colours: 1 (the default) as they are.

kind.description: A headlamp is a small area light that rides the camera.

direction.description: The way a sun's light travels.

size.description: The side of a headlamp's emitter, in metres.

world.description: Without it the background is black and lights nothing.

kind.description: One colour all round, a procedural daylight sky, or an image all round that is the background and lights the scene (an HDRI).

strength.description: The factor the colour, the sky or the image is multiplied by. A change without a target can key it (worldStrength).

backdrop.description: How bright the camera sees the world, set apart from 'strength', which is then only how strongly the world lights the scene: a sky that is seen and lights little, or one that lights and is not seen (0). Without it the camera sees the world as strong as it lights. A change without a target can key it (worldBackdrop).

image.description: Of the kind 'image': a Radiance .hdr or an OpenEXR .exr file, relative to the plan. An equirectangular picture (longitude by latitude, twice as wide as high), its upper edge overhead and its middle in the east (+X): from left to right it runs from the west by the north, the east and the south back to the west.

rotation.description: Of the kind 'image': how far the image is turned about the vertical, in degrees, anticlockwise seen from above.

texturedMaterials.description: Played by the module 'textured_materials', after 'models' and 'look': materials that drape an image over the models they name, by the models' own UV maps, and may let the scene show through. A terrain over a cave is a model with one of these.

id.description: The material's name in the scene; unique among these and look.materials.

models.description: The ids of the models that wear it. Such a model names no material of its own.

color.description: The colour without an image, and on a model without a UV map.

image.description: A .png or .jpg file, relative to the plan.

opacity.description: How solid the material is seen from its front. Default 1.

backOpacity.description: How solid it is seen from behind. Default: as from the front. 0 makes a terrain that is not there for a camera under it.

shadow.description: False keeps the models that wear it from casting shadows. Default true.

cutaway.description: Since player 1.13: a hole straight down through the models that wear it, so that a terrain shows the cave under it. The hole is every place within 'radius' of 'lines', measured across the ground (only X and Y count). The mesh stays as it is: the material lets the scene through, the same in Cycles and in EEVEE; in the draft look the faces in the hole are taken away, without the soft edge or the rim. A change's 'cutaway' keys how open it is.

lines.description: Polylines in the plan's frame, each of one point or more (one point: a disc round it); the third number of a point is not used. At most 100000 points in all.

radius.description: How far the hole reaches from the lines, in metres.

edge.description: How wide the soft edge is, in metres, inside the radius: the ground is gone at the radius less the edge and wholly there at the radius. Default 0: a clean cut.

open.description: How much of the radius is open: 0 no hole, 1 all of it (the default). The hole grows out from the lines as it opens.

rim.description: A band of the ground just outside the hole in a colour of its own, so that the opening reads. It grows in as the hole opens. Default: none.

width.description: In metres beyond the hole. Default 3.

strength.description: How much of the colour lies over the ground at the hole, fading to none a width beyond. Default 0.6.

labels.description: Played by the module 'labels', after 'camera_track': texts that turn to face the camera, and glowing balls that mark places. Every position and size is given; ids are unique among texts and markers.

color.description: The colour the texts glow in.

id.description: The text's name in the scene.

size.description: The height of the letters, in metres.

follows.description: The id of a marker the text moves and grows with, as a caption does with a marker sized byDistance: 'at' and 'size' are where it stands and how large it is while the marker has the radius it is built with.

pulse.description: Every marker grows to 'scale' times its size over 'period' seconds, again and again.

byDistance.description: Markers that keep about the same size in the picture: a marker's radius is 'factor' times its distance from the camera, kept within minRadius and maxRadius.

id.description: The marker's name in the scene.

radius.description: In metres; with byDistance, the radius the ball is built with.

changes.description: Played by the module 'changes', after the modules that make what it changes ('look', 'textured_materials', 'labels', 'annotations'): what changes while the clip runs. Each entry names a target and gives every property that changes its keys, in rising order of time: at 't' seconds the property has the key's value. Between two keys it moves as the later key's 'easing' says; before its first key a property has that key's value and after its last one it keeps it, so a single key is a value for the whole clip. A key may lie after the clip's last frame: the clip then ends on the way to it; and before its first ('t' below 0): the clip then begins on the way from it, part of the way through a move or a fade. Up to three keys of a property may fall on one frame (not of 'visible'): the first is where the value was going, the second, whose easing is 'constant', the value it has on that frame and from it on, and a third ('constant' too) the value the move to the next key starts from, which no frame shows. An entry without a target is of the scene itself (worldColor, worldStrength, worldBackdrop, worldRotation). Two entries do not change the same property of the same thing. 'reveal' is the one property that shows a target part by part: see there. Not carried: a change of a material's image.

target.description: The one thing with this id (a model, a line, a text, a marker, an annotation or a light of the plan), or every thing with this role (stated in its section, or 'model', 'line', 'label', 'marker', an annotation's kind; every light has the role 'light'). One of the two.

visible.description: When the target is shown and hidden; each key says the opposite of the one before it, and each falls on a frame of its own. Before the first key the target is the other way round: a first key that shows it at 2 seconds keeps it hidden until then. A light is shown and hidden too, but has nothing to fade: see 'energy'.

value.description: true: shown from 't' on; false: hidden.

fade.description: Seconds the change takes, starting at 't': the target appears little by little, or goes little by little and is hidden when it has gone. Default 0: at once.

easing.description: How a fade runs: evenly (linear, the default) or eased in and out (smooth).

opacity.description: How much of the target is there, over what its material lets through by itself.

value.description: 0: nothing of it; 1: as its material has it.

tint.description: A colour laid over the target's own colours (a ramp, an image, the colours of its vertices). Light and shadow fall on it as before.

strength.description: 0: none of the colour; 1: nothing but it.

scale.description: Of a model or a line only: its stretch along its own X, Y and Z axes, as the model's 'scale' has it; [1, 1, 2] doubles the heights.

offset.description: Of a model or a line only: how far it is moved from where its 'translation' puts it, in metres along the frame's axes. [0, 0, 0] is where the plan's models have it.

energy.description: Of a light of look.lights only: how strong it is, as the light's 'energy' has it. 0 puts it out: a sun that goes out as the camera goes underground.

worldBackdrop.description: Of an entry without a target: how bright the camera sees look.world, set apart from how strongly it lights the scene (worldStrength, look.world.strength). 0 is a world that is not seen and lights as it did.

worldRotation.description: Of an entry without a target: how far the image of look.world is turned about the vertical, in degrees, anticlockwise seen from above, as look.world.rotation has it. For a world of the kind 'image'.

worldStrength.description: Of an entry without a target: the strength of look.world, which the look must have. 0 is a world that lights nothing. With a backdrop set apart (look.world.backdrop, worldBackdrop) it is how strongly the world lights the scene, and the backdrop does not follow it.

worldColor.description: Of an entry without a target: the colour of look.world, which must be of the kind 'color'.

reveal.description: Of a model or a line only: the threshold it is shown by, part by part. Every vertex of the model's mesh has a reveal value (see 'revealFront.attribute'), and so has every point of a line (its strips' 'reveal'); at every moment the parts whose value lies below the threshold are there and the rest is not. The values are in units of their own (years, metres, a count), and so is the threshold. One track shows a whole cave system in the order its values give: by the date of the survey, by the survey's order, by the distance from an entrance. The target needs a material.

value.description: The threshold at 't', in the units of the reveal values.

cutaway.description: Since player 1.13. Of a model that wears a textured material with a 'cutaway' only: how open the hole is, 0 (none) to 1 (all of its radius), as that material's 'open' says for a clip without this. The hole grows out from its lines as it opens.

revealFront.description: How the edge of 'reveal' looks, for an entry that has 'reveal'. Without it the edge is a clean cut.

attribute.description: The name of the mesh attribute that holds the reveal values, one number for every vertex. Default 'reveal', which is the vertex property of that name in a PLY file; in a GLB file the attribute is spelt _REVEAL (a name of its own, as glTF asks for one), and is found under either name. A line's values are those of its strips.

edge.description: How far behind the threshold a part is wholly there, in the units of the reveal values: a part appears over this much of the threshold's way. Default 0: a cut.

glow.description: A glow behind the edge: what has just appeared shines in a colour, strongest at the edge.

strength.description: How strongly it shines, as an emission strength. Default 3.

width.description: How far behind the threshold the glow reaches, in the units of the reveal values. Default 1.

segments.description: Played by the module 'segments' (player 1.11): the plan is a movie of several scenes and has no scene of its own. Its features are segments, texts and output; 'timeline' is the movie's, and the times of 'texts' are the movie's. Each segment names the plan of a scene beside this one. The first stage renders every segment's plan into a folder of its own inside the frames folder, each in a Blender of its own, and leaves alone the segments whose frames are there already; the second lays their frames one after the other, joined as each segment's 'in' says, with the texts over them.

id.description: Unique in the plan; the segment's strip in the video editor is 'Frames.<id>'.

name.description: What the segment is called in the progress of the render.

plan.description: The plan of the segment's scene, relative to this plan. Its timeline has this plan's fps and the segment's frameCount.

frames.description: The folder of the segment's frames, inside the frames folder of the movie.

start.description: When the segment's first frame shows, in seconds of the movie: straight after the last frame of the segment before, or, with a dissolve, that much before it ends.

in.description: How the segment begins. Without it: a cut. The first segment has none.

kind.description: dip: a colour comes over the last frames of the segment before and goes from the first frames of this one. dissolve: the two segments overlap, and the picture goes evenly from the one to the other.

seconds.description: How long a dip (both halves together) or a dissolve takes: at least one frame, and no longer than the segments it joins.

color.description: The colour of a dip. Default black.

kind.description: video: <baseName>.<container>; frames: <baseName>_0001.png onwards; still: <baseName>.png of the first frame.

directory.description: Relative to the plan, or absolute. Default: the plan's folder.

render.description: False sets the output up and renders nothing: for a plan that only saves the scene ('blend'), to be rendered from that file later. Default true.

blend.description: Played by the module 'blend_file': the built scene is saved as a Blender file, before anything is rendered. In the file the render's output is named relative to the file where it lies in the plan's folder, so the folder can be moved and rendered elsewhere: blender -b scene.blend -s 1 -e 100 -a.

path.description: A .blend file, relative to the plan.

annotations.description: Played by the module 'annotations', after 'models', 'lines' and 'camera_track' and before 'changes': things that point something out in the scene. Each has a kind (a label, a callout, a marker or a photo) and an anchor, the point it is about. Everything of it is given: where it stands, how large it is, what it says or shows. An annotation is there for the whole clip unless an entry of 'changes' shows and hides it: such an entry names it by its id or its role, and its 'visible' keys, with a 'fade', are the times it appears and goes ('opacity' and 'tint' change it too). Ids are unique among everything the plan names in the scene: models, lines, labels, lights and annotations.

id.description: The annotation's name in the scene; what an entry of 'changes' names it by.

role.description: What the annotation is, for whoever looks for it in the scene, and for an entry of 'changes' that names a whole group. Default: its kind.

kind.description: outline: a line of 'width' along 'points', drawn as the plan's lines are (needs points, width). label: a text that turns to face the camera, centred on the anchor (needs text, size). callout: a text that stands 'offset' away from the anchor, with a line from the anchor to it (needs text, size, offset). marker: a glowing ball on the anchor (needs radius). photo: a picture from an image file (needs image, width). A key that belongs to another kind is refused.

at.description: The anchor: the point the annotation is about, in the plan's frame; with 'model', in that model's own coordinates.

model.description: The id of a model or a line the anchor belongs to. 'at' is then a point of that model as its file has it (a station of it), before the model's scale, rotation and translation, and the annotation goes where that point goes, also while 'changes' stretch or move the model. The annotation itself is not stretched or turned.

text.description: What a label or a callout says.

size.description: The height of the letters of a label or a callout, in metres.

radius.description: Of a marker, in metres; with 'sizeBy' the radius it is made at, which the distance then scales.

symbol.description: Of a marker; default ball. pin: a ball on a point that is on the anchor. cone: stands on its point, on the anchor. cube and ring: centred on the anchor, the ring turned to the camera. image: a small picture of 'image', turned to the camera, 2 x 'radius' wide.

sizeBy.description: Of a marker: scale it with its distance from the camera. distance: the radius is 'factor' metres per metre of distance. screen: it is seen 'factor' times the picture's width across, wherever the camera is (by the lens at the start of the clip). Either is held between 'minRadius' and 'maxRadius'.

minRadius.description: Of a marker with 'sizeBy': the smallest radius, in metres. Default a quarter of 'radius'.

maxRadius.description: Of a marker with 'sizeBy': the largest radius, in metres. Default four times 'radius'.

points.description: Of an outline: where its line runs, in the plan's frame; with 'model', in that model's own coordinates. 'at' is a point of it.

offset.description: Where the text of a callout, or the middle of a photo, stands from the anchor, in metres along the frame's axes. A callout needs one that is not zero; its text stands on the end of the line: above it when the offset points up, below it otherwise. A photo without one is centred on the anchor.

lineWidth.description: How thick the line from the anchor is, in metres. Default for a callout: a twelfth of 'size'. A photo with an offset has a line only when this is given.

color.description: The colour a label, a callout or a marker glows in. Default: cream for a text, orange-red for a marker.

strength.description: How strongly it glows. Default 1.5 for a text, 2 for a marker, 1 for a photo. A photo shows its image as a screen would, whatever the light, and lights nothing itself.

image.description: The image of a photo, or of a marker whose symbol is image: a .png or .jpg file, relative to the plan. It is drawn whole and solid; its transparency, if it has any, is not used.

width.description: Of a photo, or the thickness of an outline, in metres.

height.description: Of a photo, in metres. Default: what the image's own shape gives for 'width'.

facing.description: camera (the default): the photo faces the camera: it stays parallel to the picture and upright in it, wherever the camera is and however it is turned, so it is always seen as the rectangle it is. fixed: it faces along 'normal' and stays so, a card that stands in the scene.

normal.description: Of a fixed photo: the way it faces, out of its front. Any length but zero.

up.description: Of a fixed photo: where its top points, as near as 'normal' lets it. Default [0, 0, 1], or [0, 1, 0] for a photo that lies flat.

frame.description: A border about a photo, in the picture's own plane.

texts.description: Played by the module 'texts': what is written over the picture, in two dimensions. A plan with texts is rendered in two stages: the scene as numbered PNG frames, then those frames with the texts over them, in Blender's video editor, as the output. Places and sizes are shares of the picture: x from its left edge, y from its bottom edge, each 0 to 1. Later items lie over earlier ones.

hold.description: Seconds the movie goes on after the last frame of the scene, which stands still meanwhile: the time of an end card. A still has none. Default 0.

fromBlack.description: Seconds the picture takes to come out of black at the start, texts and all. A still has none. Default 0.

toBlack.description: Seconds the picture takes to go to black at the end. Default 0.

id.description: The item's name in the video editor; unique among the items.

role.description: What the item is: title, caption, credits ... An item with the role 'caption' is what a subtitle file would say.

kind.description: text: lines of text. box: a rectangle of one colour. arrow: an arrow that turns about its middle, with an optional letter at its tip. image: a picture from a file, laid over the frames: a photo in a corner, or over the whole picture.

image.description: Of an image: its file, a PNG or a JPEG, relative to the plan. Where a PNG is clear the picture shows through. 'width' is its width as a share of the picture's width and 'height', when given, its height as a share of the picture's height (without it the image keeps its shape); 'at' is the point of it that alignX and alignY name.

at.description: The point of a text that alignX and alignY name; the middle of a box or an arrow.

text.description: What a text says; the letter at the tip of an arrow.

size.description: The height of a text's letters, or the length of an arrow, as a share of the picture's height.

width.description: Of a box, as a share of the picture's width.

height.description: Of a box, as a share of the picture's height.

alignX.description: Which side of a text lies on 'at', and how its lines are set. Default center.

backing.description: A text on a dark box of its own.

wrap.description: The widest a text's line may be before it is broken, as a share of the picture's width. Default 0.9.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the movie at which the item appears. Default: from the first frame.

end.description: Seconds at which the item is gone. Default: never.

fadeIn.description: Seconds the item takes to appear.

fadeOut.description: Seconds the item takes to go.

slot.description: A place only one item has at a time: of the items that name the same slot, the one that started last is drawn, and an earlier one goes when it appears. Captions share one.

turn.description: Of an arrow, in rising order of time: at 't' seconds it is turned 'degrees' counter-clockwise from pointing up. Between two turns the angle changes evenly; it may pass 360. Without it the arrow points up. For a north arrow, 'degrees' is the camera's heading, clockwise from north, at that time: one turn per frame, or per pose of the camera.

counter.description: Makes a text a counter: at every frame it shows, in place of the {} in 'text', the number the threshold of a reveal has got to: a year counter over the history of an exploration. The number is cut down to 'decimals' decimals (1987.9 shows as 1987) and kept between 'min' and 'max'; after the clip's last frame it stays as it was there.

keys.description: In place of 'target': the threshold itself, as keys in the plan's time, for a plan that has no entry of 'changes' to read it from. The plan of a movie of several scenes is one: the reveal runs in the plans of its segments. Since player 1.11.

target.description: The target of the entry of 'changes' whose 'reveal' is counted, named as that entry names it. A counter has this or 'keys'.

min.description: The least the counter shows. A threshold starts below the first value there is; a counter of years should not.

easing.description: How the value gets to this key from the key before it: evenly (linear, the default), eased in and out (smooth: 3x² − 2x³ of the way at the share x of the time), or not at all, so that it jumps at this key's time (constant).

mix.description: How a colour is mixed on its way to this key from the key before it: as light mixes, straight in the plan's linear RGB (linear, the default), or as a screen mixes two colours, straight in sRGB (srgb), which is what a browser or a picture editor shows half-way. The player keys an srgb move frame by frame.

role.description: What a label or a text is, for whoever looks for it: lower-case words joined by '-'. The player stamps a label's role on its object (thide_role).
